chunks: He who has an intelligent mind looks to his goal, and knows his low road as well as his high road. The caller has called, and the shepherd has tended (his flocks). So respond to the caller and follow the shepherd.

key_terms.أَمَدَهُ: His goal / his limit / his destination
key_terms.الدَّاعِي: The caller (one who invites to God or truth)
key_terms.الرَّاعِيَ: The shepherd (one who guides the flock)
key_terms.غَوْرَهُ: His low road / the depth / the humble path
key_terms.لَبِيبٍ: Intelligent mind / one of deep understanding
key_terms.نَجْدَهُ: His high road / the elevated path

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the caller and shepherd metaphor in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) highlights the intellect (*al-labib*) as the faculty that discerns the true destination and depth of one's spiritual journey. He employs the metaphors of the 'caller' (*da'i*) and the 'shepherd' (*ra'i*) to urge believers to heed the divine invitation and follow the authoritative spiritual leader, a concept central to Shia understanding of *Imamah* and *Wilayah*. This call to action underscores the necessity of aligning one's inner perception with outer obedience to the Prophet's Household.
